method.processes: fresh process per backend per repeat
method.keys: mixed (hashed full-width), sequential (consecutive even) and clustered (runs of 1,024 consecutive even keys at scattered bases)
method.chart_statistic: 100 * (median Go operation time / median Rust operation time - 1)
method.distinct_churn: Unique keys selected by a coprime stride over the full insertion domain alternate with a disjoint key set. Every deletion must succeed with the expected value and every insertion must be fresh; checksums are independently computed by the Python harness.
method.distinct_operation_count: min(entries, queries) keys per round; rounds multiplied by floor(queries/min(entries, queries)). All recorded sizes execute 4194304 pairs.
method.replacement_validation: Serial replacements sum every bit of the previous value. Python independently computes the expected sum, accounting for duplicate queries; both drivers verify final values outside timing. Parallel replacement sums remain order-independent.
method.concurrent_contracts: Both concurrent maps omit len() and read payloads with plain loads validated by node versions. The Go Map ports the pinned Rust latched tree's protocol; the Rust implementation is unmodified.
method.string_keys: Byte-string cells write each mixed key as user: and 16 hex digits, with uint64 values: Rust String keys, Go gobbtree.Bytes ([]byte) keys, both made before the timed build. Rust's containers move the Strings in; Go's copy each key's bytes into their leaves, in buffers the collector doesn't scan, as a caller may change its slice afterwards. Rust replaces values with update and get_mut, Go with Insert; churn inserts back the String a removal returned, and Go the same Bytes. Go's Tree runs on the Map's tree as its single writer, taking no latches.
method.store: Upstream bbtree-store's examples/bench.rs at rust_source, unmodified, built with rust_flags, fat LTO and one codegen unit (it sets mimalloc as its global allocator), against store/cmd/storebench, its port. A fresh process per run, the two alternating, 3 runs per size; each record is one run's printed figures, as internal/store_compare.py parses them.
method.retakes: A CPU or store segment where one backend's three runs spread more than 1.3x, by the sum of each run's serial timings (internal/spread.py), runs again in full, both languages; internal/matrix.sh runs the matrix so.

limitations: Desktop apps (the window server, an IDE, a screen saver) kept the one-minute load average between 2.5 and 8.4 at the starts of the CPU and memory segments, and at 4.6 at those of the store segments; the machine drew AC power throughout, as logged each minute. Small timing differences are inconclusive.
Only the store segments ran at b1429f6. The CPU, string-key and memory segments are the previous run's, at 24c8dd2, whose code outside store/ is the same byte for byte.

Every CPU segment's backend spread at most 1.05x over its three runs, by the sum of a run's serial timings, max over min, and no segment was run again. The 32K store segment's first pass spread 2.00x on Rust's side and was run again, all three backends, to 1.02x; the 1M and 10M store sizes spread at most 1.04x.

Against the previous report (8215927), Go cells that moved more than 10% past Rust's change were Map's four-worker reads at 4K and 262K mixed keys, the string Map's four-worker reads at 262K, and Tree reads at 50M sequential keys, where Rust's sped up and Go's held. The previous report's driver, run beside this one afterwards in the same session, timed them alike (medians 2.25 and 2.26 ns, 4.34 and 4.35 ns, 12.03 and 12.21 ns, 61.7 and 61.0 ns), so those moves are the machine's state. Builds that moved are in the next item.

Against the previous report (24c8dd2), the one store cell of Go's that moved more than 10% past Rust's change was eight threads' inserts at 32K entries, 10.7% faster. The previous report's driver, run beside this one earlier in the same session, timed it alike (minima 115 and 114 ns), so that move is the machine's state.

Builds that take under 0.2 s, every one at 4K and 262K entries and those at 5M sequential and clustered keys, are single timings that the page faults of fresh memory dominate: a backend's three spread up to 2.1x, so those build cells are inconclusive. Builds of 0.2 s or more spread at most 1.04x. Memory segments are not retaken.

A store run times one pass over every entry, as upstream's benchmark does: at 32K entries a pass takes a few milliseconds, too short for the core's clock to settle, so single 32K cells vary, and the same cells ran up to 2x slower, both languages, in runs outside the matrix. The eight-thread cells are wall time on a shared machine.
CPU records include Go's builtin map and sync.Map at 4096, 262144 and 5000000 entries with mixed keys only.
Memory records cover Tree and Map.
